text: On cosmos_qa, we evaluated a weak-to-strong training scheme that selects training examples by agreement between weak labels and the strong model's embedding geometry. Across 10 seeds, the method attains a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.38 with a standard error of 0.03. No baseline PGR was supplied with this experiment, so the number should be read as a standalone measurement rather than as evidence of a gain over any comparison method; we make no claim that the agreement-based selection outperforms random or full-data training, since there is nothing here to compare against. The standard error of 0.03 over 10 seeds indicates the seed-to-seed spread is moderate, but it speaks only to the stability of this single configuration. The result is also limited to one testbed, cosmos_qa, and one selection criterion, so generalization to other datasets or weak-supervisor pairings remains untested. A matched baseline run would be needed to interpret 0.38 as favorable or unfavorable.
